core_obligations: Statement (lines 1760-1772): for a ring R, a differential graded R-algebra (A, d), a right differential graded A-module M', a left differential graded A-module M, and a complex of R-modules N, Hom in Mod_(A,d) from M' to Hom(M, N) equals Hom in Comp(R) from M' tensor_A M to N, where the tensor product is viewed as a complex of R-modules.

Common identification (proof lines 1774-1784): both sides correspond to graded A-bilinear maps M' x M -> N compatible with differentials; for the right hand side this is the defining property from the tensor-product section, and a given g on the left determines, via the More on Algebra composition lemma, a map of complexes g': Tot(M' tensor_R M) -> N.

Linearity transfer (lines 1785-1789): the map g' unpacks to a graded R-bilinear map g'': M' x M -> N compatible with differentials, and the A-linearity of g translates immediately into A-bilinearity of g'', which identifies the two sides.
proof_roadmap: State the common set of differential-compatible A-bilinear parametrized maps.
Unpack a left-hand-side element through the total-complex composition lemma.
Check the A-linearity transfer, concluding the equality.
difficulty_reason: Adjunction lemma (statement 1760-1772, proof 1774-1789): the module-level Tensor-Hom adjunction - the proof exhibits the same set of differential-compatible A-bilinear maps on both sides, the right side by the defining universal property of the tensor product and the left side via the standard total-complex composition lemma; the A-linearity transfer is carried out explicitly; no step is omitted. H2: standard adjunction identification.
